title: Authorization Decision Service (ADS) + adaptive enforcement middleware for API, runtime, and Console
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an Authorization Decision Service (ADS) and thin adaptive enforcement middleware that centralizes RBAC v2 policy evaluation for three ingress surfaces: public API, runtime inference gateway, and Redwood Console. ADS will expose a gRPC/HTTP v1 endpoint for decision requests, support batched queries, and return structured allow/deny metadata and audit payloads. Middleware libraries (Go for runtime, Node/TS for Console/backend API) will implement optimistic caching, policy-version pinning, fallback deny/soft-allow strategies, and local rate-limited evaluation when ADS is unreachable. Scope: design policy schema (condition expressions, resource attributes, temporal constraints), decision caching/sharding, structured audit envelopes, SSO/SAML identity mapping hooks, admin role editor integration in Console, and end-to-end tests and performance SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: ADS prototype accepts decision requests over gRPC and HTTP and returns allow/deny with structured audit_event payload
Middleware libraries exist for runtime (Go) and Console/API (Node) and integrate with existing auth chain
End-to-end latency for single decision (cold) <= 8ms p50 and <= 25ms p95 at service load profile
Decision caching reduces remote calls by >= 60% for our production trace sets without violating freshness rules
Audit events emitted conform to schema v1 and are ingested into audit pipeline (Kinesis -> ES) during integration tests
SAML assertion mapping flow tested with IdP test tenant and Console role-editor reflects ADS-managed roles
Security review completed and threat-model entry added to docs with mitigations for replay, tampering, and high-privilege escalation
comments: 2026-02-28 - Spike completed: compared PDP vs ADS models. Decided on centralized ADS with local middleware caches to minimize cross-service policy duplication.
2026-03-03 - Design review: PM (Priya Kapoor) prefers granular audit payloads for billing and compliance. UX (Jorge Silva) requested role display names and last-modified metadata for Console editor.
2026-03-05 - Implementation note: chose protobuf v3 for ADS API. Initial Go server skeleton in runtimes/authz/ads. Added feature flag ads.experimental for canary.
2026-03-08 - Perf run (DEV environment): ADS single-instance p50=6.2ms p95=18.4ms with a 500 qps synthetic trace. Memory footprint for policy cache ~120MB for 10k policy objects.

2026-03-10 - Security review request submitted (SEC-queue). Listed top concerns: audit tampering, stale cache leading to privilege leak, SAML attribute spoofing. Action: add HMAC on audit envelopes and sign decision responses.

2026-03-12 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ads/pull/2243 - contains proto, server skeleton, basic eval engine and integration tests against runtime gateway. Requesting eng-review from @maria-g and @sven-k.

Next steps: add policy compiler for condition expressions, implement sharded in-memory LRU cache with TTL per policy-version, wire audit stream to existing audit pipeline, and coordinate Console integration with design for role-editor UX.
